text:
Anna M: quick heads-up — ran into a subtle mismatch between paged/blocked KV and the new attention kernel path. kernel wants a contiguous KV span for autoregeneration but our pager hands back discontiguous slab fragments.
Simon K: can you show a repro or trace?
Anna M: yep. small example: input grows to 2.5k tokens, kv pages map like [0-1023][1024-2047][2048-3071], but fragmentation means a single key for a token can live split across slab chunks after compaction. kernel tries to memcpy a contiguous block and fails perf-wise.
Maria L: is the failure correctness or perf?
Anna M: perf mainly, but in degenerate cases kernel fallback allocs blow up latency. also eviction races can make pages transient during attention compute.
Derek: thoughts: we can either 1) provide a kernel shim that exposes a virtual contiguous view (gather into temp buffer) or 2) change pager API to provide stable pinned segments that kernel can request with scatter-gather.
Jen: option 2 sounds cleaner for long term but bigger refactor. option 1 is faster to ship.
Simon K: agree. If we do shim, need clear contracts: max-copy bytes, when to prefetch, and backpressure signals. also need to guard the kernel from page faults / evictions mid-attention.
Anna M: proposal draft: introduce PageHandle v2 with semantics: `pin()` returns an opaque handle valid for N milliseconds, `get_sglist(handle)` returns scatter-gather list of (addr,len) and `coalesce_hint(len)` suggests likely contiguous span. Kernel can call `gather_to_temp(handle, outbuf, offset, len)` if contiguous not available.
Maria L: Pinned handles plus eviction callback: pager promises not to evict pinned pages. eviction will return EBUSY if pinned and include a requeue token. That avoids races.
Derek: for perf, we should avoid copying for common cases. Add fast-path: pager keeps recent coalesced slabs for hot prefixes and can return a single contiguous pointer when possible.
Anna M: yep — add metrics: `kv.scatter_fraction`, `kernel_copy_bytes`, `pin_hold_time` to detect when we hit lots of copies.
Jen: kernel-side change: accept sglist interface and try to do in-place attention when sglist length == 1, else call gather_to_temp. also add a config: `max_copy_bytes` gated by SLO.
Simon K: we should add an async prefetch API too: when tokenization predicts upcoming seq_len, kernel can call `prefetch_pages(seq_end)` so pager pulls slabs ahead of time. reduces stall.
Maria L: prefetch + pin semantics is good. edge: what about compaction that moves live fragments? compaction must respect pinned windows or perform in-place pointer fixups. that complicates compactor.
Derek: we can scope compaction: avoid moving pinned ranges; mark them non-compactable until pin expires. compaction can run incrementally.
Anna M: implementation plan: short-term (2 sprints) shim + sglist support in kernel + eviction EBUSY; medium (4 sprints) implement PageHandle v2 & pin semantics; long-term compactor refactor.
Jen: can we get perf numbers for a 2k seq with shim vs full pinning path? need to justify copy overhead.
Anna M: i'll run microbench: baseline (no fragmentation) vs fragmented (random slab splits) vs pinned path. will post numbers here by EOD tomorrow.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: `eng-runtime/paged-kv/shim-proto` build started by Anna M — CI job #1284 queued.
Simon K: also document API in `docs/kv/paging.md` before landing so engs can adopt. add examples for async prefetch.
Maria L: one more UX note: expose a `fragmentation_warning` in console when scatter_fraction > 0.2 for a model — ops can then enable heavier pinning or QC.
Derek: ack. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the proposed interfaces and a small compatibility shim patch.
Anna M: thanks all — i'll drop the microbench and the prototype link once CI passes. :thumbsup:
Jen: :rocket:
Simon K: :thinking_face:
